actor: research director (automatable: public data only, no contact, $0)

rationale: Pre-registered verdict: inconclusive. Policy-closed PR authors replied 59.8% of the time (52/87, CI 49–69%) versus 90.2% for merged LLVM newcomers (83/92, CI 82–95%): a clear gap, but short of the ≤ 45.1% success threshold. Exploratory within-LLVM comparison: 80.9% vs 90.2%, so engagement alone discriminates weakly.
Design pre-registered before data collection: pooled policy-closed group across GitHub (LLVM alone has too few), LLVM newcomer control, fixed decision thresholds.
Rejected, and reaffirmed by follow-up evidence. 83.3% of 281 OSS AI policies permit AI in code, so AI authorship is the wrong thing to gate on. The detector space is also crowded.
Remains advanced. Follow-up evidence shows most policies require high human involvement (67.3%), which is the property this gate checks. The retrospective experiment is still the next step.
